label: prf:markov-trace-product
title: Proof of markov trace product
html:
Proof. Proof of markov trace product

Proof. The Markov trace processes the product by peeling generators from the right. At each step, \sigma_i is the rightmost (largest-index) generator in the remaining word, and the Markov property gives:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\cdots (a_i \sigma_i + b_i))
  = 
  (z \cdot a_i + b_i) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\cdots).

This works because:

  1. The chain at \sigma_i reduces to a_i \sigma_i + b_i (linear in \sigma_i and the identity).
  2. The Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n) = z\mathrm{tr}_M(x) applies to the \sigma_i term.
  3. Generator \sigma_i is the rightmost active generator, so the Markov property applies directly.
  4. The remaining word involves only \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{i-1}, independent of \sigma_i.

Applying this recursively from i = n-2 down to i = 0 gives the product formula. \square

Caveat: non-adjacent generators only

The product factorization requires that the generators \sigma_i at each reduction step are non-adjacent — that is, step 4 above (independence of the remaining word from \sigma_i) must hold. When generators are adjacent (e.g. \sigma_0 \sigma_1 \sigma_0 in the trefoil), the Yang–Baxter relation \sigma_0 \sigma_1 \sigma_0 = \sigma_1 \sigma_0 \sigma_1 creates dependencies that invalidate the factorization.

For the trefoil-like element \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 with adjacent generators \sigma_0 and \sigma_1: the naïve vertex volume product gives z^3, but the correct Markov trace (Ocneanu--Wenzl recursion) is hz^2 + z (corrected Markov trace). canonical at q_0: vertex-product z^3 \approx 0.1245 vs canonical hz^2 + z \approx 0.5514 (4.4\times off). (Earlier versions had these two values swapped; fixed.)

The product formula remains valid for the nuclear Garside element (where generators are distant) and for braids whose Hecke reduction separates generators into independent chains.
